bug_description.normalized: The staged 1048-byte witness crashes in the second `trySubset()` path of `hb-subset-fuzzer`. Its last byte is `0x20`, so `_fuzzing_alloc_state()` returns 0 and `src/failing-alloc.c` does not inject allocator faults in the reproduced run. The second trailer parser consumes the four 8-byte axis records backward: the first three calls to `hb_subset_input_pin_axis_location()` therefore use `axis_tag = 0x20202020` and `axis_value = 538976288.0f`, while the fourth uses `(tag 0x0004000c, value 0x14000200)`. The same malformed witness font's `fvar` table exposes two axes tagged `0x20202020`, so those first three lookups succeed and `hb_clamp()` forces the supplied value to the axis default `8224.12548828125`; `input->axes_location` ends up storing a default-valued point `Triple` for that tag. `hb_subset_plan_t` copies that pin, `_normalize_axes_location()` creates non-empty `normalized_coords` with zero normalized values for both malformed axes, and `pinned_at_default` stays true. That state makes `OT::glyf::_populate_subset_glyphs()` seed each `SubsetGlyph::dest_start` from `source_glyph.get_bytes()`, `Glyph::compile_bytes_with_deltas()` skip allocating replacement glyph bytes, and `SubsetGlyph::compile_bytes_with_deltas()` still set `allocated = true` from the success return. Later `OT::glyf::subset()` takes the `_add_loca_and_head()` failure exit at `src/OT/glyf/glyf.hh:133-138`; unlike the later normal cleanup, that early exit lacks the `!c->plan->pinned_at_default` guard and calls `_free_compiled_subset_glyphs(glyphs)` anyway. `SubsetGlyph::free_compiled_bytes()` then calls `dest_start.fini()`, and `hb_array_t::fini()` frees a pointer 608 bytes inside honggfuzz's 1 MiB testcase buffer, matching the saved ASan stack `hb_free_impl -> fini -> free_compiled_bytes -> _free_compiled_subset_glyphs -> OT::glyf::subset`. The fix removes these early frees by allocating `padded_offsets` before glyph compilation and deferring cleanup to the later guarded path.

evidence_note: `trace_feedback.json` required two repairs: record the reverse-read axis-pin clamp-to-default path, and remove the invalid dependency that attributed the `_add_loca_and_head()` failure predicate to the prior step. `run_flags.json` keeps `runtime_disambiguation` false and the feedback did not request it, so this Stage 02 trace remains fully source-grounded with no instrumentation. One runtime fact is still unavailable from saved artifacts: why `_add_loca_and_head()` failed on this witness. The crash stack and carried source states are nevertheless sufficient to identify the taken early-free site and the aliased pointer that reaches `hb_free()`.

source.description: First non-harness library statement on the witnessed path that resolves the reverse-read space-tag axis trailer against malformed `fvar` metadata and computes the default-valued pin later written into subset state.
source.value_from: The exact 1048-byte witness ends with four raw 8-byte axis records, then `num_axes = 4`, `flags = 0x20202020`, and a 16-codepoint text trailer. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` reads those records backward, so the first three calls into `hb_subset_input_pin_axis_location()` use `axis_tag = 0x20202020` and `axis_value = 538976288.0f`. The same malformed witness font's `fvar` table exposes two axes with tag `0x20202020`, so `hb_ot_var_find_axis_info()` succeeds for the accepted space-tag calls and supplies min/default/max values that make `hb_clamp()` resolve to the axis default `8224.12548828125`. That default-valued pin is the attacker-controlled state later stored into `input->axes_location` and normalized to zero.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `hb_array_t::fini()` frees `dest_start.arrayZ`, but on the witnessed path that pointer still aliases source-glyph bytes inside honggfuzz's testcase buffer rather than HarfBuzz-owned heap storage.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` and says the freed address is 608 bytes inside the 1 MiB region allocated by honggfuzz `util_Calloc` for testcase input. That matches `source_glyph.get_bytes()` aliasing the original readonly blob instead of a separately allocated compiled-glyph buffer.

root_cause.description: The `_add_loca_and_head()` failure exit frees compiled subset glyphs unconditionally. On the witnessed pinned-at-default instancing path, that cleanup reaches `dest_start.fini()` even though `dest_start` still aliases source-glyph bytes rather than owned heap storage.
root_cause.note: Step 1 rules out the earlier `padded_offsets.alloc(...)` cleanup because allocator-failure injection is disabled for this witness, and step 5 keeps `pinned_at_default` true so the later normal cleanup at line 145 is not taken. That makes this `_add_loca_and_head()` error exit the only `_free_compiled_subset_glyphs()` caller consistent with the saved stack. The fix removes this early free by moving `padded_offsets` allocation before glyph compilation and deferring cleanup to the existing `normalized_coords && !pinned_at_default` guarded path.

parser_admitted.description: The second `trySubset()` call has reached the variable-font glyf subsetting path. Because `normalized_coords` is non-empty here, `subset()` instantiates `font` and `_populate_subset_glyphs()` will call `compile_bytes_with_deltas()` for each glyph.

tainted_value_origin.description: This constructor copies the attacker-controlled axis pins from the subset input into the plan and initializes the default-pinned state that later governs glyph-byte ownership.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: This step consumes the non-empty `input->axes_location` produced at step 3. Because the three accepted space-tag trailer records all store the same default-valued point Triple under the same key, the copied map is still non-empty even though the fourth raw record fails lookup. If the copy were empty, `_normalize_axes_location()` would return immediately at line 881 and the later normalized-coordinates glyph path would be unreachable.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness aliases the full witness as a readonly face, disables allocator-failure injection because the last byte is `0x20`, then reads the four trailer axis records backward so the first three calls to `hb_subset_input_pin_axis_location()` use tag/value `0x20202020` and store a default-valued axis pin.

The subset plan copies that stored default-valued point Triple, initializes `pinned_at_default = true`, then creates non-empty zeroed `normalized_coords` for the malformed `fvar` axes while leaving `pinned_at_default` true.
Variable-font glyf subsetting creates `font`; each `SubsetGlyph` starts with `dest_start` aliased to source-glyph bytes from the original face blob.

Because the plan is still pinned at default, glyph-byte compilation returns success without allocating replacement header/body storage, yet `SubsetGlyph::allocated` is still set true from that success return.

The `_add_loca_and_head()` failure exit wrongly frees those pinned-at-default glyph aliases, so `dest_start.fini()` calls `hb_free()` on a pointer into honggfuzz's testcase buffer and ASan reports bad-free.

fine_trace.note: The harness materializes two vulnerability-relevant states from the exact witness. First, the last byte is `0x20`, so `_fuzzing_alloc_state()` returns 0 and `src/failing-alloc.c` stops injecting allocation failures for this run. Second, `hb_blob_create()` / `hb_face_create()` alias all 1048 attacker-controlled bytes as the source font blob. Later `source_glyph.get_bytes()` points back into this blob, so freeing it means freeing testcase-buffer memory rather than HarfBuzz-owned heap storage.

Source. In the second `trySubset()` path the harness consumes the four 8-byte trailer records backward, so the first three calls into this function use `axis_tag = 0x20202020` and `axis_value = 538976288.0f`. The same witness's malformed `fvar` table exposes two axes with tag `0x20202020`, so `hb_ot_var_find_axis_info()` succeeds for those calls and `hb_clamp()` forces the huge supplied value down to the axis default `8224.12548828125`. This step materializes the default-valued pin that later keeps normalization at zero.

The clamped default from step 2 is stored as `Triple (val, val, val)` under key `0x20202020`. The next two identical space-tag records overwrite that same map entry with the same default-valued point, while the final raw record `(value 0x14000200, tag 0x0004000c)` fails `hb_ot_var_find_axis_info()` and leaves the map unchanged. The resulting `input->axes_location` is non-empty and carries a point pin at the axis default.

The subset plan copies the accepted axis pins from step 3 into `user_axes_location` and begins from the optimistic assumption that every pinned axis stays at the default location. That `pinned_at_default = true` state later decides whether compiled glyph bytes are heap-owned or still aliases into the source blob.

Because step 4 made `user_axes_location` non-empty, this function does not return at line 881. The malformed `fvar` table reports two `AxisRecord`s and both use the same space tag stored at step 3, so the loop normalizes that same point Triple twice. For each axis `normalize_axis_value(axis_range.middle)` returns 0 because the middle value equals the axis default, so `normalized_coords` becomes non-empty `[0, 0]` and the guard at line 928 never clears `pinned_at_default`.

The non-empty `normalized_coords` from step 5 takes `subset()` into the variable-font instancing path and creates `font`. That is the control edge that makes `_populate_subset_glyphs()` call `compile_bytes_with_deltas()` for each glyph instead of leaving `SubsetGlyph::allocated` false.

The witness sets `flags = 0x20202020`, so `HB_SUBSET_FLAGS_NO_HINTING` is clear and this path seeds `dest_start` from `source_glyph.get_bytes()`. That makes `dest_start` an alias into the readonly source-face blob from step 1 before any instancing-specific recompilation happens. Because step 6 created `font`, the function immediately passes that alias into `compile_bytes_with_deltas()`.

fine_trace.code:
//dont compile bytes when pinned at default, just recalculate bounds
if (!plan->pinned_at_default)
fine_trace.note: Step 5 left `plan->pinned_at_default == true`, so this guard is not taken. That skips the branches that would allocate replacement glyph bytes, and `compile_header_bytes()` also leaves `glyph_header == nullptr` because line 148 requires `!plan->pinned_at_default`. The function still returns success, so `dest_start` remains the source-face alias from step 7.

fine_trace.code: allocated = source_glyph.compile_bytes_with_deltas (plan, font, glyf, dest_start, dest_end);
fine_trace.note: Even though step 8 left `dest_start` pointing into the source-face blob and produced no owned header/body replacement, this assignment records the successful return as `allocated = true`. Later cleanup interprets that success flag as ownership and reaches `dest_start.fini()`.

Root cause. At this point step 1 still has `alloc_state = 0`, step 5 left `pinned_at_default == true`, step 8 left `dest_start` aliased to source bytes, and step 9 set `allocated = true`. When `_add_loca_and_head()` fails at this line, the error block unconditionally calls `_free_compiled_subset_glyphs (glyphs)` instead of deferring cleanup to the later `normalized_coords && !pinned_at_default` path. The current-step failure predicate therefore makes cleanup treat aliased source bytes as owned compiled storage.

This helper walks the `glyphs` vector created in step 7 and dispatches each element to `free_compiled_bytes()`. Because the failure exit at step 10 is not guarded by `!pinned_at_default`, it applies this cleanup even to glyphs whose `dest_start` still aliases the source face.

Step 9 made `allocated` true, so this cleanup branch executes. `dest_start.fini()` therefore runs on the aliased source-glyph pointer preserved by step 8, even though that pointer was never returned by HarfBuzz allocation code for this glyph.

Sink. At this point `arrayZ` is still the source-glyph slice from steps 7-8, not a heap buffer owned by `SubsetGlyph`. `hb_free()` therefore receives a pointer into honggfuzz's testcase buffer, and ASan reports `attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` at this line.

format.name: 1048-byte `hb-subset-fuzzer` witness whose reverse-read axis trailer pins malformed space-tag axes at default while allocator faults are disabled
format.contract: Exactly the 1048-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_59592/poc` (sha256 `80c7801d8fa64e8b21eb937e0b7f3dab46e083dc26bf3c1cdcee8be7f2d0dc8a`). Byte 1047 is `0x20`, so `_fuzzing_alloc_state(data, size)` returns 0 and `src/failing-alloc.c` does not inject allocation failures in the reproduced run. Bytes 944..975 hold four raw 8-byte axis records in forward buffer order: `(value 0x14000200, tag 00 04 00 0c)` then three `(value 0x20202020, tag 20 20 20 20)` pairs. The harness loop at `test/fuzzing/hb-subset-fuzzer.cc:102-117` consumes those records backward, so its first three calls to `hb_subset_input_pin_axis_location()` all use `axis_tag = 0x20202020` and `axis_value = 538976288.0f`, and the fourth uses the non-matching `0x0004000c` tag. The same witness font's malformed `fvar` table at byte offset 936 reports two axes with tag `0x20202020`; those first three lookups therefore succeed and `hb_clamp()` resolves each supplied value to the axis default `8224.12548828125`, so `input->axes_location` ends the loop with a non-empty default-valued point `Triple` for that tag. `_normalize_axes_location()` then produces non-empty zeroed `normalized_coords` while leaving `pinned_at_default` true. Later `OT::glyf::subset()` takes the `_add_loca_and_head()` failure exit and frees `dest_start`, which still aliases source glyph bytes inside honggfuzz's testcase buffer. This contract is limited to this exact staged witness and this observed second-`trySubset()` path, not all malformed variable-font inputs or all axis trailers.
